content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert: GPU serving queue growth detected across gpu-pool-02, autoscaler attempts failing. Error rate spiking on /v1/generate to ~8.6%. PagerDuty: https://pd.example/tickets/PD12345

alice: oncall here, ack. pulling up dashboards and kube state. beginning triage. anyone already looking at node logs?

mike: i'm on it. seeing a flurry of CUDA/Xid errors and OOM kills on nvidia-driver pods - nodes are flapping NotReady which prevents the autoscaler from stabilizing and adding new capacity.

carla: can we cordon+drain the worst nodes to stop churn and shift traffic to healthy nodes? also want a quick impact estimate for customers.

alice: cordoning 3 nodes: gpu-node-12, gpu-node-15, gpu-node-18. starting drain now (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data).

devops-bot: autoscaler attempted scale up to 10 -> 12 gpus at 20:07:45Z but provisioning failed: "instance creation error: node provisioning timeout"

mike: paste of dmesg from gpu-node-12 showing repeated Xid errors:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568123] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x24:0x0:850)
[ 1234.568456] Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=4321, vc=0
[ 1234.569000] oom-kill: killing process 9876 (python) total-vm:...
```
Looks like driver/kernel mismatch under memory pressure -> kernel OOM + driver reset.

sophie: quick mitigation suggestion: set autoscaler to ignore nodes in NotReady for 5m and try to provision in a different zone, plus throttle incoming requests to non-essential tenants.

alice: throttling config applied to non-enterprise routes: rate-limit middleware bumped down to 0.5 r/s for background tenants. Notifying SRE and CS for customer comms.

mike: rolling a driver daemonset restart with fallback to older driver (530.41 -> 525.85) across affected nodes. kubectl set image daemonset/nvidia-driver nvidia-driver=image:525.85-hotfix && kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-driver

carla: doing canary restart on gpu-node-20 first. monitoring.

devops-bot: kube events: node gpu-node-20 moved Ready (kernel driver reloaded) at 20:12:10Z

alice: after restart: queue length dropped from ~11k to ~700 within 6 minutes, error rate down to 0.9%, tail latency improving. still keeping autoscaler paused for 10m to avoid flipflop.

mike: confirming Xid messages dropped on sampled nodes. will keep rolling replacement across the remaining flapping nodes.

carla: impact summary for PS/CS: approx 25 minutes of elevated errors/latency between 20:03-20:28Z. High-traffic customers A + B saw increased 95p latency and some 5xxs — flagged for outreach.

alice: escalation/handoff: i'll stay on until 21:00Z to finish verification then hand to night oncall. assigning post-incident owner: carla for root-cause and remediation items.

carla: initial RCA hypothesis: recently rolled driver kernel module (530.x) had an edge-case memory leak under sustained KV-cache pressure leading to kernel OOM and GPU reset (Xid 79). Autoscaler exacerbated by treating flapping nodes as failed and choosing same zone where provisioning capacity was constrained.

sophie: proposed action items:
- pin driver version in deployment manifests and add preflight smoke tests (owner: mike)
- tweak autoscaler backoff & cross-zone fallback (owner: infra team)
- add healthcheck for Xid/OOM pattern to auto-cordon before kube sees NotReady (owner: eng-sre)
- customer notifications + SLA check (owner: cs)

alice: good. creating incident tracker and paging list now. Status: mitigated -> monitoring. will postmortem with timeline + metrics. :white_check_mark:

devops-bot: incident PD12345 closed by alice at 20:35:12Z (auto-comment: mitigated, monitoring).

mike: leaving logs and a gist of diagnostics here: https://internal/gists/PD12345-diagnostics (contains driver logs, node health metrics)

carla: assigning postmortem doc to /product/infra/postmortems/PD12345-driver-reset-memory-leak - will include runbook changes.

alice: thanks team. thumbs up to rapid cordon/drain + rollback. follow-ups scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
